chapter: Jelly Roll Morton and other records
title: Only one trumpet and one clarinet on the Morton records
summary: Mitchell is sure he was the only trumpet and Simeon the only clarinet, rejecting rumors of Lee Collins or extra clarinets.

bands.name: Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Oh, while I think of it on those records, uh, once Lee Collins told me that he played... I know he made an old autograph date on a different label, a small company autograph. Mm-hmm. He made a tune called Fishtail Blues, which they later called Sidewalk Blues. Mm-hmm. But was there ever any other trumpet player on those Jolly Roll records beside you, that worked with you? Or worked with me? No. That they used more than one? No. No. No. No, I can't, no, I don't think we... Because you were the only one. That's what I thought from hearing them, I didn't know. Yes, yes, yes. There was never, never but, uh, just the one trumpet. But Lee got some people mixed up by telling him that he made records with Jolly, so they thought maybe he and you were on together. Oh, yes, yes.
But you weren't. No, no, no, because, uh, whenever I, uh, I, there wasn't any, he only had one trumpet when he, when I was there.

And I wondered about the clarinets, because on the Sidewalk Blues and the Dead Man Blues, it sounds like they're two clarinets or so. And Simeon, we know, is on all of them. And somebody said that, uh, Bigard or, uh, Darnell Howard or somebody might have had two or three clarinets.
Do you remember that on any of them? No. No, I don't remember that, no. No, I can't remember anybody but, uh, Simeon.

Simeon. Simeon. Uh-huh. On the clarinet. No. Because one of them would sound, one of them sounds like, sort of in the trio part, they get soft down low. Uh-huh. It may be you playing with them down low too, that sounds full harmony going along. Yeah, yeah, yeah.

Like there might be another clarinet, I thought. No, no, uh, when I was with him, he only had one clarinet and one trumpet. One trumpet. One trumpet. Uh-huh. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, I'm pretty sure. I can't remember having any more than one trumpet or one clarinet.
